mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months compresses the discount rate for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS has declined for 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% within the past 3 months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes a recession and causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high industrial production growth (INDPRO > 102.0), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to overheating and potential monetary tightening, resulting in negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO exceeds 102.0, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A positive quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) indicates robust economic expansion, which typically supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with positive GDPC1 growth, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI inflation rate above 3.5% signals persistent inflation, which typically leads to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates an active monetary tightening cycle, which typically causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL fails to produce negative 5-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a labor market cooling regime (UNRATE rising above 4.0% and PAYEMS growth slowing), the S&P 500 tends to decline over the next 60 trading days due to recessionary pressures.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE rises above 4.0% and PAYEMS growth slows, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.
